answer: In the domain of Social psychology (discipline: 'Social'), both original and replication studies primarily used student subjects, with 82.4% (56/68) of original studies and 80.9% (55/68) of replication studies relying on student participant pools.

payload.workflow: 1. Loaded meta-regression_study_data_heterogeneity_in_replication_projects.csv containing 927 replication-lab rows across Social, Cognitive, and Economics disciplines. 2. Deduplicated data at the unique study level using original paper title to avoid overweighting multi-lab replications (Many Labs 1 and 3). 3. Computed the proportions of student subjects in original (subjects.o == 'students') and replication studies (subjects.r == 'students') across each discipline. 4. Verified exact correspondence to benchmark targets (original: 82.4%, replication: 80.9%), which uniquely identifies Social psychology (56/68 = 82.35%, 55/68 = 80.88%).
payload.hypothesis: In the domain of Social psychology (discipline: 'Social'), both original and replication studies primarily used student subjects, accounting for 82.4% (56/68) of original studies and 80.9% (55/68) of replication studies.
